seo_title: Make.com vs Zapier: Enterprise API & Workflow Audit (2026)
meta_description: Technical comparison of Make.com and Zapier for high-volume JSON parsing, RBAC, and enterprise-grade automation scalability.
direct_verdict: Make.com is the superior choice for high-volume, complex JSON data manipulation due to its granular control and cost-efficiency. Zapier wins for organizations prioritizing rapid deployment, ease of use, and deep native integration with 9,000+ apps.

comparison_matrix.product_a_spec: Native visual array/object mapping with iterators
comparison_matrix.product_b_spec: Linear step-based mapping with limited array handling

comparison_matrix.product_a_spec: Role-based access with team-level folder permissions
comparison_matrix.product_b_spec: Advanced admin controls, SCIM, and SAML SSO

comparison_matrix.product_a_spec: Operation-based, scales linearly with data volume

comparison_matrix.product_b_spec: GDPR, SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, ISO 27001

comparison_matrix.product_a_spec: Visual error routing and retry logic per step
comparison_matrix.product_b_spec: Automated replay and basic error notifications

product_a_pros: Superior data manipulation via native iterators and aggregators
Advanced visual branching and error handling logic
product_a_cons: Steeper learning curve for non-technical users
Lacks enterprise-grade SCIM/SAML provisioning in lower tiers
product_b_pros: Unmatched library of 9,000+ pre-built app integrations
Enterprise-ready security features including SCIM and SSO
Extremely low barrier to entry for non-developers
product_b_cons: Task-based pricing model penalizes complex multi-step workflows
Limited ability to manipulate raw JSON payloads compared to Make
hidden_gotchas: Buyers often overlook that Zapier's task-based pricing counts every single step in a workflow as a task, meaning a 10-step process consumes 10 tasks per execution, leading to exponential cost growth. Conversely, Make.com users frequently underestimate the complexity of maintaining custom HTTP modules, which require manual API documentation reading and header management, unlike Zapier's plug-and-play connectors. Both platforms hide significant costs in 'Premium' app tiers, where specific high-value integrations are gated behind higher subscription levels.
